results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
I built a four-color creature ramp deck (green, white, blue and a red splash). It's a brew: no published list has played these three cards together.

**The plan:** Mana creatures ramp you into big creatures, and The Jolly Balloon Man copies the best one. The copy enters again, so its "when this enters" effect happens twice, and the copy has haste.

**How the three cards work together:**
- **Bloom Tender** gives one mana for each color among your permanents.
- **Balloon Man** is red and white, so he adds two colors to that count.
- **Sewer-veillance Cam** is a blue permanent that costs one mana, so it adds a fourth color. You can cast it at instant speed, and when it enters it untaps Bloom Tender, so the Tender taps twice in one turn (about 8 mana).

**The main way to win (aimed at turn 5):**
1. Turn 1: Llanowar Elves.
2. Turn 2: Bloom Tender.
3. Turn 3: Balloon Man.
4. Next turn: flash in the Cam, which untaps the Tender for a second tap.
5. With that mana, cast Nature's Rhythm with X=8 to put Craterhoof Behemoth onto the battlefield, or just cast Hoof.
6. Use Balloon Man to copy Craterhoof. The flying, haste copy gives your team a second +X/+X and trample.

**Other things to copy:**
- Ouroboroid: two copies of its counters trigger at combat.
- Explosive Prodigy: its damage to a creature happens twice.
- Brightglass Gearhulk: it searches up two cards that cost 1 or less, including the Cam.

**Directions I considered:**
- **A pile of other cards that count your colors** (Kithkeeper, Shinestriker, Aurora Awakener). Too many seven-drops with no proven base.
- **A white-blue-red value deck around creatures with "when this enters" effects.** It loses the mana that Bloom Tender is built for.
- **The Aang deck's green-white ramp creatures and its Nature's Rhythm + Craterhoof finish, plus red.** I chose this one. It already has the fast mana and the single big payoff that Balloon Man doubles.

**Changes from that shell:**
- The menu's Selesnya and Landfall lists run Badgermole Cub, but the card tool shows it's banned in Standard, so I left it out.
- I didn't change the land mix much. I added red through Starting Town, Stomping Ground and Sacred Foundry.
- There are 22 lands, which matches real Aang lists.

**Honest odds** (no mulligans, on the play, by turn 5):
- Bloom Tender alone: about 57%. Balloon Man alone: about 57%.
- Tender, Balloon Man and a Cam or Gearhulk together: 22.5%.
- Balloon Man plus something good to copy: 54%.
- Drawing every card in the full Craterhoof line naturally is very rare. The deck relies on Nature's Rhythm and Gearhulk to find pieces instead.

The 15-card sideboard uses cards Aang lists already carry: graveyard hate for Reanimator and Dimir Excruciator, removal and counters.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) Dwarves and Equipment deck. It's a brew: no published list from the last 400 days plays these three cards together, and none of them shows up in recent results.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Boros Aggro shell:** borrow its burn spells (Burst Lightning, Shock) and its mana base, and swap its creatures for Dwarves.
2. **Boros Weapons artifact shell:** Weapons Manufacturing and artifact tokens to reach the storied count. It shares almost nothing with Dwarves.
3. **A deck all-in on Dwarves and Equipment:** every creature a Dwarf, every artifact an Equipment, plus Burst Lightning and the Boros dual lands.

**What I chose:** Direction 3. Dáin's Company already forces red-white, and it, Kíli and Mauler all reward the same two card types. The Weapons artifacts would just be cards Company can't find.

**The plan:**
- **Turn 1:** Dwarven Mauler. If Leyline Axe is in your opening hand, it starts on the battlefield for free.
- **Turn 2:** Kíli. The Axe's equip cost of 3 drops to 1 on Mauler, making it a 3/2 with double strike and trample that hits for 6.
- **Turns 2–3:** Your many legendary Dwarves (Thorin, Giott, Bofur, Dáin Ironfoot) plus your Equipment quickly reach the 3 artifacts or legends that turn on Kíli's storied ability. After that, your first equip each turn is free, and Thorin gives all your creatures and artifacts ward {1}.
- **Turn 4:** Mjölnir deals 4 damage to a blocker, then goes on Giott for free (or 1 mana). Giott has double strike and Mjölnir doubles its damage, which ends most games by turn 5.

**What the requested cards do:**
- **Dáin's Company** is your consistency card. About half the deck (30 of 60 cards) is a Dwarf or Equipment it can pick up from the top four, and it gains lifelink once you have another Dwarf.
- **Kíli** draws a card off nearly every play and makes equipping free.
- **Mauler** makes the Axe and Chainsaw cost only 1 to equip.

**Notes:**
- **Chainsaw:** The checker flagged it because no recent Standard deck plays it. I kept it because it's both removal (3 damage when it enters) and an Equipment. Company can find it, it triggers Kíli and Giott, it counts toward storied, and Mauler equips it for 1.
- **Odds:** The submit tool reports about 0% for drawing every card in the win line by turn 5. That number requires all 7 named cards at once and doesn't count Company's digging. The deck really needs one carrier plus one Equipment: by turn 4 you've seen at least one of the 11 Equipment (counting Dáin Ironfoot, who makes an Axe token) 89% of the time. Mauler and Kíli are each about 53% by then, so many games will use a different Dwarf as the carrier.
- **Mana:** 22 dual-heavy lands with 19 red and 19 white sources. The checker found no issues against real Boros Aggro lists.
- **Sideboard:** Aimed at the decks on your list: Lightning Helix and Sear for Prowess and Elementals, Hexing Squelcher so control can't counter your spells, Shattered Acolyte (a Dwarf) and Abrade to destroy problem artifacts and enchantments, and Ghost Vacuum for graveyard decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built an Orzhov sacrifice deck around your three cards and submitted it as a brew. The mana is borrowed from the format's Lifegain lists.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Orzhov sacrifice, using the Voice of Victory package from the menu.** Voice of Victory is in 306 recent lists (7.9% of the field), mostly in Mardu Discard, Lifegain and Azorius Blink.
2. **Mono-black Rats/Treasure** with cards like Common Crook and Undercity Dire Rat.
3. **Golgari Food** with Scavenger's Talent and Experimental Confectioner, using the Badgermole Cub / Llanowar Elves base from the menu.

**Why the Orzhov version:** The Sackville-Bagginses only drains when you sacrifice a *token*, and Voice of Victory makes two 1/1 Warrior tokens every attack that you have to sacrifice at end of turn anyway. White also adds the cards that pay off every sacrifice (Popular Egotist, Vito, Kambal) and the format's best cheap removal (Erode).

**The plan:**
- **Setup:** Greedy Freebooter (dies into a Treasure), Umbral Collar Zealot (a free sacrifice outlet), and Sackville's enter trigger (sacrifice something, draw a card, make a Treasure) give you a stream of Treasures, Clues and Warriors to cash in.
- **Damage:** Each token sacrificed makes the opponent lose 1 life from Sackville and 1 more from Popular Egotist. Egotist's lifegain then sets off Starscape Cleric for another point, so with all three out, one token is 3 damage. Kambal, Vito and Tolls of War add damage and make more tokens.
- **Protection:** Voice of Victory stops opponents from casting spells during your turn, so they can't interrupt with instant-speed tricks while you sacrifice everything in one big turn.
- **Removal:** Requiting Hex, Erode and Bitter Triumph keep the fast decks (Prowess, Landfall) in check.

**Honest odds:**
- By turn 3 on the play, you'll have both a sacrifice outlet and a token maker 77.5% of the time.
- The exact six-card line I submitted (Freebooter, Zealot, Sackville, Egotist, Voice, Cleric) is all drawn by turn 6 in under 1% of games. The deck doesn't need that exact sequence, though: any outlet plus a token maker plus one payoff already deals damage every turn.

**Things to know:**
- The mana is 22 lands, matching the Lifegain shell, and the deck passed the format check with no warnings.
- I ran only 3 Sackville-Bagginses because it's legendary: a second copy would die to the legend rule.
- The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the graveyard and control decks in the current field.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
I built a Boros Superfriends Tokens brew (red-white walkers protected by tokens). No published list in the last 400 days plays these three cards together, so this is new ground. It passed the deck check and was accepted with 24 lands, 21 white sources and 19 red.

**The plan:** Gideon's Memorial comes down on turn 2. Its mana can only be spent on planeswalkers, which lets you cast a 4-drop walker on turn 3, Elspeth, Storm Slayer on turn 4 and Ajani Unrelenting on turn 5. It also gives creature tokens +1/+0 and vigilance, so tokens can attack and still stay back to protect your walkers.

**What the three cards you asked for do here:**
- **Ajani Unrelenting** is the finisher. It makes a 2/2 Cadet token whenever you activate a loyalty ability on any of your walkers, not just Ajani. Elspeth doubles every token you make. Ajani's −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens, so with a board made of tokens it only hurts your opponent. The next turn, its +1 gives your army +1/+0 and haste.
- **Solitary Cell** is your answer for 2 mana: it exiles any of the opponent's nonland permanents costing 3 or less. Later, it turns spare legendary cards into new cards. The deck has 16 legendary cards for this (walkers and Memorials).
- **Gideon's Memorial** also has an emergency mode: discard it to deal 4 damage to an attacking or blocking creature.

**The other cards:**
- **Ajani, Outland Chaperone:** makes a token every turn, and its −2 kills a tapped creature.
- **Resolute Reinforcements:** flash blockers to protect your walkers.
- **Caretaker's Talent:** draws a card when your tokens enter.
- **Removal:** Burst Lightning, Lightning Helix and Get Lost.
- **Mana:** the land base is borrowed from Boros Dragons, the most-played red-white deck in the results. The deck check flagged it for having no blue, black or green sources, but those only show up in Dragons lists because of a land that can count as any type. They don't matter here.

**Directions I considered:**
1. Jeskai Control, taking the Stock Up / No More Lies package from the menu, with walkers as finishers.
2. Go-wide Boros tokens built around Voice of Victory and other token creatures.
3. **Boros Superfriends, which I picked.** It's the only one where all three cards feed each other: Memorial ramps and pumps, the walkers keep making Cadets, and Ajani's sweeper only hits the other side.

**Honest odds:** Drawing every card in the full line by turn 6 happens in only about 5% of games. By turn 5 you'll have a Memorial about 57% of the time and an Ajani Unrelenting about 46% of the time (no mulligans). The deck doesn't depend on the exact line, though: any walker making tokens behind the removal does the same job.

The 15-card sideboard covers Reanimator, cheap threats, Prowess and control decks with counterspells.

Turn 3: +1 for a Kithkin token each turn (a 2/1 vigilant one with Memorial); -2 kills a tapped attacker
Turn 4 off Memorial mana: doubles every token, so +1 makes two Soldiers, and Ajani Unrelenting's Cadet triggers come in pairs
Turn 5 off Memorial mana: -3 deals 4 to every creature except your tokens, a one-sided sweeper. Every loyalty ability you activate, on any of your walkers, makes 2/2 Cadets (doubled by Elspeth)

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery.
results.text:
I built a Jeskai control deck that splashes black for Inevitable Defeat. Tablet of Discovery speeds you into Jeskai Revelation. It's labeled a brew.

**The plan:** Early on, cheap burn (Fiery Impulse, Sear, Lightning Helix) and No More Lies keep you alive while you play Tablet on turn 3. Tablet's {R}{R} for instants and sorceries, plus Great Hall of the Biblioplex's any-color mana for spells, gets you to Jeskai Revelation around turn 5. Revelation does almost everything at once: it bounces a threat, deals 4 damage, makes two Monk tokens, draws 2 and gains 4 life. Inevitable Defeat is an exile spell that can't be countered and drains 3. Flashback lets you cast Revelation a second time from the graveyard. You win with the Monks, Helix and Revelation damage, and Great Hall turning into a 2/4 creature.

**Direction chosen:** I looked at three directions:
- **Mardu control (chosen):** The research showed that all three cards are played together in one deck: Standard's 4C Control (163 lists, running about 4 Tablet, 4 Revelation and 3 Defeat). I moved that shell to Pioneer and added the UW Control package from your menu (4 No More Lies, Consult the Star Charts, Supreme Verdict). The mana uses Pioneer's triomes, shocklands and fast lands.
- **Izzet Phoenix style:** I rejected this one. It would use graveyard recasting with Flashback around Revelation, which is too inconsistent.
- **Mardu midrange with Thoughtseize:** I rejected this too, because Tablet's mana only pays off with a deck full of instants and sorceries.

The Mardu control version won because it's the only one of the three with a proven engine behind it.

**Things to know:**
- **Mana:** The land count (26) and color sources match Standard 4C Control (about 27 lands, 9 black sources), not Niv-Mizzet. I ran the land check against Pioneer's Niv-Mizzet deck, but that's an 80-card list with 35 lands, so its "add lands" warning doesn't apply here.
- **Black:** There are 9 black sources for Defeat, and 4 of them are Great Halls, which can make black for instants.
- **Sear:** The deck checker flagged Sear because almost nobody plays it in Pioneer. I kept it because it's an instant, so Tablet's mana can pay for it. It kills Screaming Nemesis, Badgermole Cub, Greasefang and Kaito, which the 1-mana burn can't. Fatal Push isn't realistic on a 9-source black splash.
- **Odds:** On the play, you have about a 60% chance to draw at least one Tablet by turn 6, and the same for Revelation, before Stock Up and Consult dig for them. You'll have both together about 35% of the time. Neither is in recent Pioneer results, so this is untested in the format.
- **Sideboard:** The 15 cards target the top decks in your menu: Rest in Peace and Kutzil's Flanker for graveyard decks, Pyroclasm, High Noon and Brotherhood's End for prowess, and Dovin's Veto, Negate and Teferi for control.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Tolarian Terror, Bushwhack and Eddymurk Crab.
results.text:
I built this as **Simic Spells-Tempo**. No published list in the last 400 days runs all three of your cards, and the only recent Pioneer Crab list is an Izzet deck, so this is a brew.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Temur Crab:** the Izzet Crab list plus Bushwhack. That means three colors, and Bushwhack would mostly just fetch lands.
2. **Sultai:** borrow Fatal Push and Thoughtseize from the Golgari/Dimir decks. But Thoughtseize is a sorcery, so it can't help you flash in Crab at the end of the opponent's turn, which is the Crab's main strength.
3. **Simic (chosen):** borrow the blue cheap-spell package from the Izzet Prowess and Phoenix decks (Consider, Sleight of Hand, Flow State, Stormchaser's Talent) and add green. I picked this because it's two colors, and green turns your 5/5s into removal. Bushwhack's fight mode and Ram Through let a 5/5 kill a creature, and Stubborn Denial becomes a hard counter once you have a creature with 4+ power.

**The plan:** 29 cheap instants and sorceries fill your graveyard. Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab each cost 1 less for every instant and sorcery card there, so you can cast a 7-drop for 1–3 mana around turns 3–5. Early on, Bushwhack fetches a land. Once a 5/5 is out, Bushwhack and Ram Through use it to kill their best creature. You can flash in Crab at the end of their turn; a copy cast on your own turn taps two blockers. Stubborn Denial and Spell Pierce protect the threats while about 10 power finishes the game in two attacks, typically around turn 7.

**Odds:** With 8 copies of the two 5/5s, you'll have at least one by turn 4 on the play 79% of the time.

**Choices worth knowing:**
- **Lands:** I run 19. The checker suggests 23.6, but it counts Terror and Crab as full 7-drops; for comparison, Izzet Prowess averages about 19.7. There are 29 one-mana spells, many of them card draw, plus Bushwhack and Growth Spiral to find lands.
- **Ram Through and Growth Spiral:** The checker flagged both as almost never played in Pioneer, and I kept them anyway. Ram Through is your only instant-speed removal: the 5/5 deals 5 damage and takes none back. Growth Spiral draws a card and puts a land into play, so you can cast a 5/5 and still keep Denial mana open the same turn.
- **Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks in the field:
  - Pick Your Poison for the Greasefang deck's Parhelion II
  - Aether Gust for red Prowess and green decks
  - Ghost Vacuum for graveyard decks
  - Negate and Mystical Dispute for UW Control
  - Essence Scatter and Disdainful Stroke for Sheoldred and other big threats
